thread.title: Close Update: Buying Erupts Into The Close as Wall Street Positions For Mid-Term Results

author: MT Newswires
title: Close Update: Buying Erupts Into The Close as Wall Street Positions For Mid-Term Results
text:
Shutterstock photo Wall Street's market averages closed at their session highs as upbeat earnings and bullish labor market data kept stocks afloat while investors waited for election results that could galvanize President Donald Trump's pro-business, trade-protectionist policies. Led by gains in Caterpillar ( CAT ), Boeing ( BA ) and International Business Machines ( IBM ), the Dow closed above its 100-day moving average for the first time in three weeks.
Early defensiveness dissolved at the NYSE open as market participants shifted focus away from the election uncertainties to encouraging quarterly results and a rebound in the tech sector with Apple ( AAPL ), Facebook ( FB ) and Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) higher for the first time in several days.
Data on the labor market was also a factor in today's positive price action as the number of available jobs continues to outstrip available workers. According to the monthly job openings and labor turnover survey (JOLTS) open positions declined slightly in September to 7.009 million from an upwardly revised 7.293 million (7.136 million initially) in August.
Demand for risk was evidenced by cheaper gold prices and the Treasury 10-year note cracking the 3.20% yield threshold. A very well received 10-year note auction (with the exception of anemic demand from direct bidders) drove the yield to a four-week high of 3.22%. Higher borrowing costs failed to dent the mood on Wall Street as the small-cap Russell 2000 closed at its highest level since mid-October.
While Wednesday's price action will likely reflect the outcome to the election (a split Congress is seen as bearish for Wall Street), the start of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting will also come into focus. The FOMC is not expected to raise interest rates at the policy meeting conclusion Thursday, but their statement will be gleaned for clues for the timing of the next hike.
